title: getRouteHeaderConfig('/compliance-vault') resolves to the Evidence Management header, not a distinct Vault header
description: routeHeaderMapping.js has a static entry for '/compliance-vault' (icon HardDrive, iconColor green.400) whose title/subtitle are literally 'Evidence Management' / 'Secure repository for compliance evidence' — identical in content to the '/evidence-management' entry's purpose. There is no page.jsx under src/app/(private)/compliance-vault backing this route.
steps: Inspect the returned title, subtitle, icon and iconColor fields
expectedResult: Returns { icon: HardDrive, iconColor: 'green.400', title: 'Evidence Management', subtitle: 'Secure repository for compliance evidence' } — confirming the config aliases the vault route's chrome to Evidence Management rather than defining vault-specific copy.

title: isValidPermission() rejects 'compliance_vault.*' and 'vault.*' as unknown permission strings
description: permissions.js's MODULES/NAV_MODULES lists (src/config/permissions.js) enumerate 'evidence', 'evidence_collectors', 'evidence_mapping', 'trust_vault' among others — there is no 'compliance_vault' or 'vault' module anywhere in the catalog. isValidPermission() falls through to MODULES.includes(mod) && ACTIONS.includes(action), which is false for any compliance_vault.* string.
preconditions: permissions.js loaded in isolation for unit testing
expectedResult: All three calls return false — no distinct compliance-vault permission module exists in the RBAC catalog; whatever data compliance-vault displays is governed entirely by the pre-existing 'evidence.*' permissions.

title: Evidence model rejects a 'certificate'-type document whose metadata.expirationDate is not after metadata.effectiveDate
description: evidence.model.js's pre-save hook validates that metadata.expirationDate must be > metadata.effectiveDate for any evidence document (type enum includes 'certificate' and 'attestation', which is the closest thing to a certification record inside the vault-adjacent evidence store). This is the only expiry validation compliance-vault content has access to — it has no dedicated certification schema of its own.
preconditions: An Evidence document instance with type='certificate'
steps: Set metadata.effectiveDate = 2026-08-01 and metadata.expirationDate = 2026-07-01 (expiry before effective)
expectedResult: Mongoose pre-save validation throws/rejects the save with an error indicating expirationDate must be after effectiveDate; the document is not persisted.

title: Evidence status enum used by the vault workflow screen matches featureWorkflows.js's defined states
description: evidence.model.js's status field comment states 'Synced by WorkflowTransitionService — must match featureWorkflows.js states', enum: ['draft','submitted','assigned','under_review','needs_revision','closed','expired','archived']. Any vault-context workflow UI (e.g. a hypothetical /compliance-vault/evidence/[id]/workflow screen) reading this field must handle all 8 states, since it is reading the same collection evidence-management writes to.
steps: Import the evidence status enum from evidence.model.js
Import the corresponding state list from featureWorkflows.js
Assert the two sets are identical
expectedResult: The 8 status values are identical in both places — no state exists in one definition but not the other, so a vault workflow view will never encounter an evidence status it cannot render.

title: GoogleDriveIntegrationCard.handleViewDetails() constructs a '/compliance-vault/integrations/google-drive' URL with no evidence page backing it
description: GoogleDriveIntegrationCard.js:136-138 hardcodes router.push('/compliance-vault/integrations/google-drive'). Unit-level check of the handler's pure URL-construction logic (independent of whether the route resolves) to guard against silent changes that would make this even harder to detect end-to-end.
steps: Render GoogleDriveIntegrationCard with a configured/enabled status
Invoke the component's handleViewDetails handler (via the 'View Details' button click)
Capture the argument passed to the mocked router.push
expectedResult: router.push is called with exactly '/compliance-vault/integrations/google-drive'. (Paired e2e case CPVT-E2E-002 verifies this path has no corresponding page and confirms the current broken-link behavior.)

title: vault.service.js's VAULT_ADDRESS/VAULT_ROLE_ID (HashiCorp Vault for cloud-posture secrets) are never referenced by any evidence/compliance-vault code path
description: vibrantix-backend/src/services/vault.service.js implements HashiCorp Vault AppRole auth + KV v2 secret storage exclusively for cloud-posture provider credentials (VAULT_KV_MOUNT defaults to 'cloud-posture'). The name 'Vault' is coincidental with the GRC 'Compliance Vault' feature and is a real risk for a future engineer wiring compliance-vault code to the wrong 'vault' module. This unit test statically asserts no evidence/compliance-vault module imports vault.service.js.
steps: Statically scan src/modules/evidence/**/*.js and any future src/modules/compliance-vault/**/*.js for `require(...vault.service...)`
expectedResult: No matches — confirms the two 'vault' concepts (HashiCorp secrets vault vs. compliance evidence vault) remain fully decoupled in the codebase.
